clue.text: Cheerless — wet and rainy without a break

definitions.meaning: bleak and dismal, as a dark cold season feels

definitions.text: wet and rainy without a break
definitions.meaning: describing weather of the cold season, rain on rain

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: bleak cold-season weather is gloomy in mood and also relentlessly damp.

clue.text: Country music composer

definitions.meaning: a nation, the island state west of Britain
John ... was an English composer of the early twentieth century

explanation.surface: A country-and-western songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country music' looks like the genre; split it, and 'Country' is a nation while 'music composer' is John Ireland, an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation's name doubles as the surname of the English composer John Ireland.

clue.text: Unit for heating the small room

parts.note: RM is the standard abbreviation for room, signalled by small

explanation.surface: Someone describes a heater that warms the little spare room.
explanation.walkthrough: THERM was the British gas-supply billing unit, equal to 100,000 British thermal units.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heat once used for billing domestic gas in Britain.

clue.text: Love of fiction

definitions.meaning: a love affair, a passionate relationship
a story genre, especially tales of chivalry or love

explanation.surface: Someone who adores reading novels.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an amorous affair and a genre of imaginative storytelling.

clue.text: Maxim could create PR image

indicators.note: the letters could create something new, signalling that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slogan might be dreamt up to polish someone's public relations image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could create' rearranges the letters of PR IMAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short witty saying, which is what a maxim or pithy aphorism is.

clue.text: Push in if it's out? Correct

indicators.note: out suggests the phrase is out of order, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether shoving into a queue is acceptable, and says it is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if it's out' rearranges PUSHIN. 'Correct' is a verb here, as in correcting a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct someone in the old disciplinary sense is to discipline or chastise them.

clue.text: Charity proving that virtue is effective

parts.note: virtue is goodness, the good
something that is effective works

explanation.surface: A claim that giving to good causes shows that moral virtue gets results.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable deeds done for others are called by this phrase, especially in religious usage.

clue.text: Article on Rodin's mongrel dog

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A grammatical article written about the sculptor Rodin's crossbred hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mongrel' rearranges RODIN into DIRON. A firedog is a metal stand holding logs in a hearth, so 'dog' is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This hearth support is also called a firedog, and dog alone names it.

clue.text: Sort of key post for just a few employees

parts.note: a skeleton key opens many locks
a staff is a pole or post

explanation.surface: A locksmith's description of a key and a job vacancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' suggests a job, which suits the employee theme, but it is a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum workforce kept on to run things during holidays or strikes.

clue.text: We hear top player is to step down

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis draw

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a leading player is going to retire.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a position or territory, yielding it to another.

clue.text: Bookmaker not at work will, but it doesn't matter

definitions.meaning: a bookie who is off duty offers no betting prices
an idiom for something being of no importance

explanation.surface: An off-duty bookie shrugs that the outcome is unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: A bookmaker at work sets the betting prices; one not at work sets none.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a thing changes nothing, while literally a resting bookie sets no prices.

clue.text: A local pump attendant

parts.note: reads like a garage worker at a petrol pump, but local means pub and the pump is a beer pump

explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British slang for a neighbourhood pub; the pump is the handle that draws beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub server who works the beer pumps behind the counter.

clue.text: Final decision on most recent fashion

definitions.meaning: the concluding, authoritative say on a matter
the latest style, the very newest thing

explanation.surface: A ruling about the latest style.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the definitive say in an argument and the latest trend.

clue.text: Fans present in stand run riot

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
to run riot is to go wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: being present means being here

explanation.surface: Supporters at a match go wild in the stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fans' looks like the subject of the surface sentence, supporters rioting, but it is the definition; 'run riot' gives ADNTS and 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers or supporters of a cause or team, as fans are.

clue.text: Eternal pursuit of the happy ending

parts.note: ever means for all time, eternally
in pursuit of something is to be after it

explanation.surface: The never-ending search for a fairy-tale conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Fairy tales end 'and they lived happily ever after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales close with the couple living happily this way, so the phrase stands for that finale.

clue.text: Eccentric cheerleader at head of column

indicators.note: at head of puts the first piece in front of the next
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rank is a line of soldiers

explanation.surface: An oddball pom-pom girl leading a marching column.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'cheerleader' must be split: 'cheer' gives its first letter by 'leader', and 'at head of' puts that before RANK.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd or obsessive person is called a crank, an eccentric.

clue.text: Drink was unfinished — a half of bitter

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter
a half of the word here is its second half

explanation.surface: A pub drinker didn't finish half a pint of bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts WAS to WA; 'a half of' takes TER, the back half of BITTER, which is a British ale.
explanation.definitionFit: The most basic beverage, something to drink.

clue.text: What I am when I have one over the eight?

definitions.text: What I am when I have one over the eight?

parts.note: as can mean when, at the time that
one more than eight is nine; the phrase is also British slang for being slightly drunk

explanation.surface: A drinker admits how foolish they become after one drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one over the eight' is British slang for a drink too many, and the drunk feels silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and foolish, as a tipsy drinker becomes.

clue.text: Unusual instances happening all the time

indicators.note: unusual suggests an odd arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Strange occurrences keep cropping up constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges INSTANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Unceasing, continuing without pause, so occurring constantly.

clue.text: Revealed how even CID can be manipulated

indicators.note: manipulated means worked about, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An exposé of how even the detective branch is open to corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be manipulated' rearranges EVEN and CID; CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To show or display a quality clearly is to have shown or revealed it.

clue.text: Contracts for polar missiles

parts.note: N for north, one of the poles
arrows are missiles shot from bows

explanation.surface: Agreements to supply weapons for Arctic use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' is a verb: something that narrows contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: To become tighter or thinner, as a thing that grows less wide.

clue.text: Zodiac sign that includes a shrewish woman

indicators.note: includes puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Virgo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An astrologer's sign said to cover bad-tempered women.
explanation.definitionFit: A domineering, scolding woman, the old word for a shrew.

clue.text: His second mate gets him into trouble

definitions.text: His second mate gets him into trouble

parts.words: His second mate gets him into trouble
parts.note: reads like a ship's officer causing problems, but the mate is a spouse taken while still married

explanation.definitionFit: A man who marries a second wife while still wed to the first commits a crime.

clue.text: Not fit to be a company member?

parts.note: to be in a firm is to belong to a company
to be in a firm is to belong to a company

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are unsuited to joining a business.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags reading the answer as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak or sickly in body, especially through age, so unwell.

clue.text: He uses the air rifle incorrectly

indicators.note: used incorrectly, the letters are out of their right order

explanation.surface: A man fires an air rifle wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' rearranges RIFLE; 'air rifle' tempts as one phrase but 'air' goes with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: One who flies through the air, a pilot or aviator.

clue.text: Movement of aircraft, if regulated

indicators.note: regulated means ordered anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Flights are moved under supervision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulated' rearranges AIRCRAFT and IF; the whole clue also describes what controllers regulate.
explanation.definitionFit: The planes moving through airspace, which controllers regulate.

clue.text: The first person to study a work of art

parts.note: I is the first person singular pronoun
to con is to study or pore over

explanation.surface: Someone was the first to examine a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred painting, especially an Orthodox devotional image, is such a work.

clue.text: A place to drink or eat out when he's away from home

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order
away from takes the named letters out of the word

parts.note: the he of he's

explanation.surface: Somewhere to have a drink or meal when he is not at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges OR EAT into TEARO; 'away from' takes HE out of HOME, leaving OM.
explanation.definitionFit: A café serving tea and light refreshments.

clue.text: Pay attention to sermon

definitions.meaning: to tackle or deal with a matter
a formal speech, such as a preacher's talk

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is urged to listen to the preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to deal with a problem and a formal speech delivered to listeners.
